dossier.purpose: Litestream is a Go daemon/CLI that replicates SQLite databases for disaster recovery. It monitors each database's WAL, writes changes as immutable LTX files, compacts them through levels (L0 raw, L1 30s, L2 5m, L3 1h, L9 snapshots; compaction_level.go:9-19) and uploads them to one replica destination per database: local file path, S3/S3-compatible, GCS, Azure Blob, SFTP, WebDAV, NATS JetStream or Alibaba OSS (cmd/litestream/main.go:1378-1413). `litestream restore` rebuilds a SQLite file from the replica (latest state, a TXID or a timestamp) into an explicitly chosen output path, from either a config entry or a bare replica URL (cmd/litestream/restore.go:25-116). Scope per the code: SQLite databases only. The command set (databases, info, list, ltx, register, replicate, reset, restore, start, status, stop, sync, unregister, version; main.go:250-265) contains no language-runtime or CLI-tool installer and no dotfile/config-sync function. Client-side (age) encryption config is rejected in this version (main.go:1356-1363); S3 server-side encryption options exist (s3/replica_client.go:118-126).

claims.claim: Litestream is a standalone disaster recovery tool for SQLite.
It runs as a background process and safely replicates changes incrementally to another file or S3.
Litestream only communicates with SQLite through the SQLite API so it will not corrupt your database.
Installation instructions and documentation are on the Litestream web site (litestream.io); the README itself contains no install commands.

When replication begins, Litestream creates an internal `_litestream_lock` table in the source SQLite database; it is used to acquire SQLite's write lock around WAL checkpoints; the writes occur in rolled-back transactions so no rows are left.

The table is part of the source database, so the source schema backup and restored databases also contain it; a database under Litestream should not be expected to remain byte-identical to its pre-Litestream state.
Do not drop `_litestream_lock` while Litestream is running; restarting Litestream recreates the missing table automatically.
Report security vulnerabilities privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting, not public issues; see SECURITY.md.
Bug reports, fixes and patches are welcome; see CONTRIBUTING.md.
The README (69 lines, read in full) makes no statements about encryption, supported platforms, telemetry/network requirements, MCP, or restore usage; those facts below come from code and docs.

readme.telemetry_and_network: README says nothing about telemetry or network needs (README.md:1-69). Code: (1) No telemetry/analytics/update-check/phone-home code found (searches for telemetry, analytics, sentry, posthog, update check matched only the Azure SDK ApplicationID 'litestream' User-Agent option, abs/replica_client.go:139-141, and the S3 client prefixing User-Agent 'litestream', s3/replica_client.go:924-933). (2) Network use is only to the configured replica backend; `file` replicas need no network (cmd/litestream/main.go:1379-1382); S3/GCS/Azure/SFTP/WebDAV/NATS/OSS need their service plus credentials; with no AWS keys set the SDK default chain may query instance/ECS/web-identity credential sources (s3/replica_client.go:421-445). (3) Optional outbound call: `heartbeat-url` HTTP GET to a user-set URL, only when configured and all databases synced (heartbeat.go:45-66; store.go:711-743; replicate.go:270-276). (4) Optional listeners, all off by default: Unix control socket (server.go:24-31), Prometheus /metrics when `addr` is set (replicate.go:351-367), MCP HTTP server when `mcp-addr` is set (replicate.go:182-189). (5) No Litestream account, licence or hosted service is required; cloud backends need provider credentials supplied by config keys (main.go:1127-1128,1150-1160), env AWS_*/LITESTREAM_* (main.go:2051-2065; s3/replica_client.go:230-240; abs/replica_client.go:145-155), SDK default chains (AWS shared credentials/instance roles s3/replica_client.go:421-445; GCS ADC gs/replica_client.go:86; Azure DefaultAzureCredential abs/replica_client.go:192), an SSH key file (sftp/replica_client.go:143-154) or credentials embedded in sftp/webdav/abs URLs (main.go:1822-1830,1885-1891). Config files expand $VAR / ${VAR} unless -no-expand-env is given (main.go:640-647,2105-2108); the shipped etc/litestream.yml has credentials commented out (etc/litestream.yml:1-3). No code that persists credentials was found; local state is a per-database metadata directory with suffix '-litestream' (litestream.go:20,87-90).

code.architecture: Root package: db.go (DB: opens SQLite via modernc.org/sqlite, forces WAL mode, creates _litestream_seq/_litestream_lock tables, monitors WAL, checkpoints, writes LTX files; db.go:1046-1099), replica.go (Replica: uploads LTX, Restore, CalcRestorePlan, follow mode, RestoreV3 for v0.3.x-format replicas, integrity check, level validation), store.go (Store: multi-DB coordination, compaction levels, snapshots, retention, heartbeat, validation), compactor.go and compaction_level.go (merge LTX files via ltx.NewCompactor; default levels L1 30s/L2 5m/L3 1h, snapshot level 9), replica_client.go and replica_url.go (ReplicaClient interface and URL-scheme factories), server.go (Unix-socket HTTP control API plus pprof), heartbeat.go, leaser.go + s3/leaser.go (S3 conditional-write lease interface; not referenced from db.go, replica.go, store.go or cmd/litestream), v3.go and wal_reader.go, vfs.go and vfs_config.go (VFS). Backends are one package each with a replica_client.go: file/, s3/, gs/, abs/, oss/, sftp/, webdav/, nats/ (plus mock/ and internal/ for logging, locks and resumable readers). cmd/litestream holds the CLI and all config parsing. Depends on github.com/superfly/ltx for the LTX format and modernc.org/sqlite (pure-Go SQLite) (go.mod:30,35; AGENTS.md:3). Dedup/verification as implemented: compaction keeps the newest version of each page when merging LTX files (docs/LTX_FORMAT.md:137; compactor.go:158-167); no content-defined or cross-file chunk deduplication code was found. Direct restore path: CalcRestorePlan then ltx compactor into a .tmp file then atomic rename (replica.go:686-765).

code.security_policy: SECURITY.md: report privately via GitHub private vulnerability reporting; asks for description, reproduction steps, impact and suggested fix; best-effort acknowledgement with no stated SLA (SECURITY.md:5-26).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:8-10 - replicates changes incrementally 'to another file or S3'.
claim_checks.evidence: Code supports eight replica types: file, s3, gs, abs, sftp, webdav, nats, oss (cmd/litestream/main.go:1378-1413), so the README understates scope; exactly one replica per database is enforced (main.go:786-796). Incremental LTX files per sync are written at db.go:2141-2158 and compacted per compaction_level.go:9-19.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:10-11 - Litestream only communicates with SQLite through the SQLite API so it will not corrupt the database.
claim_checks.evidence: The SQLite API (modernc.org/sqlite via database/sql) is used for PRAGMAs, bookkeeping tables, checkpoints and the long-running read transaction (db.go:1046-1099, 2596-2602). The code also opens the -wal file directly and reads it with os.Open/ReadAt (db.go:1866, 2044, 2308, 2373) and reads the main DB file through its own long-lived file descriptor (db.go:1059, 2324, 2382). The 'will not corrupt' guarantee cannot be checked statically; the repo has integration/soak/race test jobs (commit.yml:180-204, nightly-stability.yml:38-113).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:24-29 - an internal `_litestream_lock` table is created in the source DB and its writes are rolled back.
claim_checks.evidence: Matches for the lock table: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _litestream_lock (db.go:1089-1093) and inserts only inside a transaction that is rolled back (db.go:2596-2602, 2626). README omits that Litestream also forces `PRAGMA journal_mode = wal` (db.go:1077) and creates `_litestream_seq`, which is persistently upserted by autocommit statements (db.go:1085, 1567-1570).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:31-39 - restored databases also contain the lock table; not byte-identical to pre-Litestream state; restarting recreates a dropped table.
claim_checks.evidence: Restore rebuilds the whole database from LTX page data (replica.go:738-753), so schema objects including `_litestream_lock` are carried (inferred from code; no test read). Restart recreation: DB.init runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (db.go:1091) and is called when the sync executor is created (db.go:1930-1938). Non-identical bytes are consistent with init adding WAL mode and two tables (db.go:1077, 1085, 1091).

claim_checks.claim: Not a README claim - config schema exposes `age: identities/recipients`, implying client-side encryption of replicas (cmd/litestream/main.go:1182-1186).
claim_checks.evidence: The settings are rejected at startup: 'age encryption is not currently supported, if you need encryption please revert back to Litestream v0.3.x' because the feature was removed in the LTX refactor and would otherwise write plaintext (main.go:1356-1363); covered by cmd/litestream/main_test.go:574-626. Non-test Go code mentions encryption only in this rejection and in S3 SSE-C/SSE-KMS support (s3/replica_client.go:118-126, 527-556, 696-701, 872-881).

claim_checks.claim: docs/LTX_FORMAT.md:26,256-294 - LTX files are 'Checksummed: Integrity verification built-in' (CRC-64).
claim_checks.evidence: Checksum logic lives in the external module github.com/superfly/ltx (go.mod:30), which was not opened. Every LTX writer in this repo sets ltx.HeaderFlagNoChecksum (db.go:2148, 2869; compactor.go:165; replica.go:746; vfs.go:791); the docs only list the constant (docs/LTX_FORMAT.md:82). In-repo checks: periodic `validation.interval` and `verify-compaction` only test TXID contiguity and log warnings (replica.go:1782-1846; store.go:863-927; compactor.go:194-233); post-restore PRAGMA quick_check/integrity_check is opt-in, default none (restore.go:41,76-85; replica.go:1332-1366).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:15-16 - installation instructions are on the litestream.io web site.
claim_checks.evidence: The site is outside the working directory and was not opened. In-repo install text exists only in the GoReleaser release-notes header (.goreleaser.yml:132-153).
Consistent with the repo: tag v0.5.17 (.git/packed-refs:2), library API 'not considered stable' (_examples/library/README.md:6-8), VFS extension labelled Experimental (.goreleaser.yml:155).

claim_checks.claim: CONTRIBUTING.md:92-93 and docs/VFS.md:40 - build needs Go 1.24+ (VFS doc: Go 1.21+) with CGO enabled.
claim_checks.evidence: Code differs: go.mod requires go 1.25.0 with toolchain go1.25.14 (go.mod:3-5); release binaries build with CGO_ENABLED=0 (.goreleaser.yml:13-14) and AGENTS.md:3 states pure-Go, no CGO required. benchmarks.what: Idle CPU usage of `litestream replicate` to S3 after the S3 transport fix (PR #993) versus v0.5.6, measured with tests/cpu-usage/test-cpu-usage.sh
benchmarks.value: ~0.0067% with the fix vs ~0.7% for v0.5.6 (described as a 99% improvement)

risks: No client-side encryption in this version: `age` config is rejected at startup (cmd/litestream/main.go:1356-1363; test cmd/litestream/main_test.go:574-626). Only provider-side S3 SSE-C/SSE-KMS exists (s3/replica_client.go:118-126, 527-556, 872-881), so Litestream itself applies no encryption for file/GCS/Azure/SFTP/WebDAV/NATS/OSS replicas.

Scope is SQLite databases only with exactly one replica destination per database (main.go:786-796, 1050-1066; AGENTS.md:15). No code was found for installing language runtimes/CLI tools from a manifest or for dotfile/config transfer (command list main.go:250-265); backups are not general application-state archives, and cross-file or content-defined deduplication code was not found (only page-level merge during compaction, docs/LTX_FORMAT.md:137).

Enabling replication changes the source database: forces `PRAGMA journal_mode = wal`, creates `_litestream_seq` (persistently updated) and `_litestream_lock` tables (db.go:1077, 1085, 1091, 1567-1570); README discloses only `_litestream_lock` (README.md:24-35).

Verification is limited and mostly opt-in: restore integrity check defaults to `none` (restore.go:41); periodic validation checks only TXID contiguity (store.go:863-927); LTX checksum behaviour sits in the external superfly/ltx module while all in-repo LTX writers set ltx.HeaderFlagNoChecksum (db.go:2148, 2869; compactor.go:165).

Default history window is short: snapshot retention 24h and L0 retention 5m (store.go:60-72; etc/litestream.yml:52-60), and Litestream deletes expired remote files itself unless `retention.enabled: false` (etc/litestream.yml:62-65; store.go:113-116), bounding point-in-time restore.

Network surfaces and insecure-by-option settings: the MCP HTTP server (when `mcp-addr` is set) has no authentication in code and exposes restore (caller-chosen output path, replica URL, config path) and reset tools (cmd/litestream/mcp.go:52-64,183-241,322-346); the metrics listener passes a nil handler (http.DefaultServeMux) while net/http/pprof is imported, so pprof handlers are reachable there (replicate.go:11,361-366; inferred from Go semantics, not run); SFTP skips host-key verification when `host-key` is unset, warning only (sftp/replica_client.go:130-133); `skip-verify` disables TLS verification for S3 (s3/replica_client.go:406-408).

Release integrity: archives ship SHA-256 checksums.txt and SBOMs (.goreleaser.yml:101-103,189-190) but signing is disabled: `signs:` commented out (.goreleaser.yml:173-187), GPG step gated on an env var no workflow defines (release.yml:47-53), macOS/Windows signing jobs commented out (release.yml:214-291); no cosign/attestation steps found; Docker images set provenance/sbom (release.docker.yml:49-50,78-79); no dependabot/renovate config.

Maintenance and coverage: beta status (README.md:3); library API unstable (_examples/library/README.md:6-8); maintainers generally decline large external feature contributions (CONTRIBUTING.md:20-22); Go tests run only on Linux runners and no workflow runs -tags vfs tests (commit.yml:33-47,149-178); abs/ and sftp/ have no package test files; Windows is 'NOT an officially supported platform' (.goreleaser.yml:128); docs drift on build prerequisites (CONTRIBUTING.md:92-93 vs go.mod:3-5).

checks.note: main.go:316 has MCPAddr `yaml:"mcp-addr"`. replicate.go:183-188 calls NewMCP and Start only when MCPAddr != "", so only the replicate daemon starts it. mcp.go:39-45 registers seven tools, named at :84, 106, 184, 245, 260, 297 and 323. mcp.go:48 uses server.NewStreamableHTTPServer, wrapped only by httplog.Logger. Start (:52-64) is a plain http.Server with no auth. Every handler runs exec.CommandContext(ctx, "litestream", ...), which uses PATH lookup (:96, :235 and others). Makefile:71-75 has fly mcp wrap/proxy with --bearer-token. The README (69 lines, read in full) never mentions MCP.

checks.statement: The config schema exposes `age: identities/recipients`, but verified = no: the settings are rejected at startup ('age encryption is not currently supported, if you need encryption please revert back to Litestream v0.3.x') because the feature was removed in the LTX refactor and would otherwise write plaintext. A test covers this. Non-test Go code mentions encryption only in this rejection and in S3 SSE-C/SSE-KMS support.
checks.note: main.go:1183-1186 defines Age.Identities and Age.Recipients under yaml 'age'. main.go:1361-1362 rejects either one with the quoted error, and the comment at :1356-1360 gives the plaintext rationale. The check runs at startup via NewDBFromConfig (main.go:805). Global age settings are copied to each replica by SetDefaults (main.go:1330-1336), so they are rejected too. main_test.go:574-626 is TestNewReplicaFromConfig_AgeEncryption; its RejectBoth subtest actually ends at :631, which is a trivial range trim. Grepping non-test Go for 'encrypt' finds only s3/replica_client.go (SSE-C/SSE-KMS) and cmd/litestream/main.go (S3 SSE keys at :1141/:1146, plus the age plumbing and rejection). All cited s3 ranges line up.
